memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, and said to them, 'Come here; carry your cousins outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary.' So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses said." - Lev 10:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Still in their tunics. The priestly garments they had been so carefully dressed in are still on their bodies as they are carried out.

It is a devastating detail. The robes did not protect them.

There is a sober truth here that has nothing to do with condemning these particular men, whose hearts we cannot know. It is simply this: position is not the same as protection. Ordination, church membership, ministry, reputation, religious clothing of any kind — none of it substitutes for a heart that genuinely reverences God.

Jesus warned about this directly: Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name...?" Then I will tell them plainly, "I never knew you" (Mtt 7:22-23). Paul warned of people having a form of godliness but denying its power (2 Tim 3:5).

This is not meant to make sincere believers anxious. If you are worried about it, that concern is itself a sign of a heart turned toward God.

But it is meant to make all of us honest. What God wants is not the tunic. It is you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I relying on any religious position or reputation rather than on a real relationship with God?
2. Does my private life match what my public role suggests?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want the appearance of faith without the reality. Search me, and make my heart genuinely Yours. Amen.
